name: demonstrative adjectives
title: Spanish Demonstrative Adjectives Practice: Este, Ese, Aquel Quiz
description: Practice Spanish demonstratives: este, ese, aquel and their forms, pronouns and esto, eso, aquello, with a rule table and 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Spanish has three distances where English has two. Este (this) is near the speaker, ese (that) is near the listener or a little away, and aquel (that over there) is far from both. Each agrees with the noun: este libro, esta mesa, estos libros, estas mesas. Esto, eso and aquello refer to an idea or an unknown thing.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.example: este carro, esta casa, estos días, estas fotos

rules.use: Near you or not far: that, those
rules.example: ese libro, esa silla, esos zapatos, esas llaves

rules.use: Far from both: that one over there
rules.example: aquel edificio, aquella montaña, aquellos años
¿Qué es esto? Eso no es justo.

rules.use: Time: aquel for the distant past
rules.example: En aquella época no había internet.

quiz.after: zapatos que tienes en la mano?
libros de mi mochila pesan mucho.
quiz.why: In my backpack, close to me: estos.
An unknown thing: esto, the neuter form.

quiz.before: No me gusta esta chaqueta. Prefiero
quiz.after: que está allí, junto a la puerta.
quiz.why: A little away from me: esa.

quiz.after: tiempos, mis abuelos vivían en el campo.
mañana me levanté a las cinco.

mistakes: Using este for everything: Spanish separates ese (near you) from aquel (far away), and native speakers notice the difference.
Making the neuter agree: «este es mi problema» is fine, but «¿qué es este?» about an unknown object should be «¿qué es esto?».
Forgetting gender with tricky nouns: esta mano, este día, esa foto, ese problema.
Adding -o for masculine: «esto libro» should be «este libro»; esto never goes before a noun.
Writing old accents on pronouns: since 2010, «este», «ese» and «aquel» as pronouns need no accent unless there is real ambiguity.

heritage: Many heritage speakers in the US use ese and aquel naturally but rarely write them. Two writing points: esto, eso and aquello never go before a noun, and older textbooks put accents on pronouns (éste, ése) that current spelling rules no longer require.
teacher: Place three objects at three distances in the room. Students point and say Este lápiz es rojo, ese cuaderno es azul, aquella mochila es negra, and then move objects to change the forms.

faq.question: What is the difference between ese and aquel?
faq.answer: Ese is near the listener or at a middle distance; aquel is far from both speaker and listener, in space or in time. In everyday Latin American speech, ese often covers both, but aquel is still common for the distant past.

faq.question: When do I use esto, eso and aquello?
faq.answer: When you do not know the name of the thing (¿qué es esto?) or when you refer to an idea or a whole situation (eso es imposible). They never go before a noun and have no plural.

faq.question: Do demonstrative pronouns have an accent?
faq.answer: Not anymore by default. The 2010 spelling rules removed the accent from este, ese and aquel used as pronouns. You may still see éste or ése in older books.
